name: Venetium (Windows RT)
author: hamed7ir
description: Venetium is Chromium 150 (150.0.7871.226) for old ARM Windows tablets. This is the thumb2 build for the original Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1, on the Surface RT (Tegra 3) and Surface 2 (Tegra 4). Windows RT only runs Thumb-2 code, so I ported V8, the JavaScript engine of Chromium, to Thumb-2, and the JIT is on. It's built on Supermium and ungoogled Chromium, and it's a PGO and ThinLTO build. I tested it on my Surface RT with Windows RT 8.1: pages, scrolling and video work, and the sandbox is on. Telegram Web and Discord work too, and so does casting to a TV. RT 8.0 should work, but I haven't tested it on a device yet, and there it draws in software, because RT 8.0 has no Direct3D shader compiler. Qualcomm devices like the Lumia 2520 no longer crash at start, but they still need testers. It has a built-in ad and tracker blocker (EasyList and EasyPrivacy) that is on by default. On Windows 10 build 15035, use the normal ARM32 build, Venetium. It's faster there.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
Run Venetium-Setup-150.0.7871.226-win8-8.1-arm32-thumb2.exe. It installs for your user only, with shortcuts and an uninstaller, and doesn't need admin.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from 1.3: close Venetium, then install 1.3.2 over it.
The ad and tracker blocker is on by default. To allow a site, use the "ads blocked" icon in the address bar, or turn the blocker off in chrome://settings/content/ads.
If a video stops playing, start Venetium with --disable-features=VenetiumArm32CodecSteering and tell me the site.
